hpi: The patient is found to have Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease. This disease predisposes patients to renal failure and increases the chances of urinary symptoms. Not recognizing this diagnosis could lead to a family history of renal insufficiency, patients could be misdiagnosed as having nephrolithiasis, and they may require different management. The patient should be referred to a MRA. Indications for MRA include a family history of renal failure, agents to rule out other pathology, and the patient should be counseled on the importance of screening. The patient should be counseled on their family history, as it is reasonable to get a MRA in this case.
